Hathaway, Aeroballistic Range Tests of the Basic Finner Reference Projectile at Supersonic Velocities, DREV-TM-9703, Defence Research Establishment Valcartier, August 1997 (DTIC ADA636861): Table IX, 'Six-degree-of freedom aerodynamic coefficients - Multiple fits' (PDF pp. 48-49), Fig. 2, 'Model configuration' (PDF p. 53), and sections 3.1 (the model, PDF p. 16) and 5.2 (the fits and the moment reference, PDF pp. 22-23). reading: Typed from the printed table, each cell checked against a 110-dpi render of the page. Each row is one multiple fit: two to four free flights at one nominal Mach number reduced together by a six-degree-of-freedom fit, given at their average mid-range Mach number. cn_alpha is the table's CNa and cm_alpha its Cma, the linear terms of the normal-force and pitching-moment coefficients, per radian (the report's derivatives are with respect to the sine of the angle of attack), on the body's cross-section pi d^2/4, the moment about the reference point 5.50 calibers aft of the nose tip (section 5.2). The report's nomenclature gives the reference area and states no reference length; the body's diameter d is taken (ADR-351). cn_alpha_probable_error_percent and cm_alpha_probable_error_percent are the fit's probable errors as the table prints them, in whole percent (the table prints '0.%' for the moment's). The fits' cubic terms, CNa3 and Cma3, are both held at 0 on these six rows (the table solves for Cma3 only at its two rows above Mach 3.5), so each slope is a linear fit over the angles flown. mean_squared_yaw_deg2 is the table's DBSQ, the fit's mean squared yaw in square degrees. The two rows above Mach 3.5 (3.734 and 4.300) are outside the project's envelope and are not typed.

geometry.note: Fig. 2, in calibers of the body's diameter, 30.0 mm: a cone of 10 degrees half-angle 2.84 calibers long on a cylinder, 10.0 calibers overall; four rectangular fins 1.0 caliber in chord and 1.0 in span, flush with the base; each fin drawn as a single wedge in section, sharp at the leading edge (radius 0.004) and 0.08 calibers thick at its trailing edge (section 3.1 calls the fins 'conical in shape with a thickness of 0.08 cal at the base'), canted 0, 2 or 4 degrees; the nose tip's radius 0.004; the center of gravity 5.50 calibers from the nose tip.
